title: Riverlight
description: Soft bands of river green, warm sand and terracotta create a landscape that sits somewhere between a place and a memory. Marr invites you to slow down and notice where one colour gives way to another.
detail: The curved forms suggest a river without describing a particular location. Notice the small orange circle: its warmth changes how the surrounding greens appear. There is no prescribed reading; it might feel like sunlight, a distant landmark, or a point of attention.

title: Soft Form No. 3
description: An imagined clay sculpture brings two rounded forms into a delicate balance. Its open centre makes the space around the object part of the work.
detail: Walk around the piece and imagine how the opening would change from each angle. The contrast between a grounded base and a lifted curve explores weight, balance and the appearance of softness in a solid material.

title: The Blue Hour
description: Layers of blue and a pale horizon evoke the suspended moment between day and night. Small variations in the surface reward a longer look.
detail: The horizon is intentionally difficult to locate. The work asks whether a landscape can be remembered through colour alone. Try looking first at the darkest area, then at the lightest, and notice how your sense of depth changes.

title: Quiet Geometry
description: A playful arrangement of circles, arches and blocks turns simple shapes into an unexpected conversation.
detail: Each shape is flat, yet overlapping edges suggest depth. Follow the repeated arch across the composition. The print explores how repetition can create rhythm without exact symmetry.

title: Botanical Notes
description: A collection of imagined plant studies records the small differences between leaves, stems and the spaces they leave behind.
detail: Fine lines sit alongside broader washes of green. The drawing values close observation over scientific classification. Look for a pair of leaves that appear similar at first but differ in their direction or scale.

title: Afterimage
description: Translucent coloured panels overlap to suggest a changing architectural space. The installation explores the relationship between colour and memory.
detail: The layered planes invite different views rather than a single correct vantage point. In this sample gallery, Room 05 is reached by stairs; choose a step-free tour to explore the other works.
